mainTopic: Bodily dignity in תפלה and קריאת שמע: רבי's conduct, praying aloud, passing wind, and reciting near nakedness or filth
overview: The amud opens by finishing the description of רבי's conduct during תפלה. A ברייתא seems to condemn the same things he did, such as yawning, sneezing and spitting. The גמרא reconciles each one: רבי yawned involuntarily, sneezed from the nose (only 'sneezing from below' is a bad sign), and absorbed his saliva discreetly in his clothing, as רב יהודה rules. רב הונא then limits the ban on praying aloud: it applies only to someone who can concentrate quietly, and never in a ציבור. A story about רבי אבא, who was about to leave for ארץ ישראל, brings a ברייתא about passing wind during תפלה: one waits for the smell to pass, and one version adds stepping back and a humble prayer. The גמרא then turns to קריאת שמע. It discusses reciting in bed with a barrier at the neck or at the heart, and argues over reciting while walking through filthy alleys. There, רב הונא's report permits it with a hand over the mouth, while רב חסדא strongly refuses, and a ברייתא supports each side. Harsh verses condemn someone who keeps reciting when he must stop, and a verse promises long life to one who stops. The amud ends with רב הונא's ruling, supported by a ברייתא, that a garment tied around the waist permits קריאת שמע.

steps.title: How רבי behaved physically during prayer
steps.stepSummary: The report on רבי's conduct in תפלה ends. He would touch or adjust his garment but would not rewrap himself, and he covered his chin when he yawned.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he would feel around in his garment, but he would not wrap himself up again. And when he yawned, he would put his hand on his chin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a report of what רבי did while praying: some small physical actions were allowed, and some dignity was kept. This report sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the report, רבי is described yawning, sneezing, and spitting during תפלה. Here we learn the limits he kept. He handled his garment, for example to remove a bothersome louse, but he did not stop to rewrap himself. When he yawned, he hid his open mouth with his hand.

keyTerms.meaning: touches or feels around (here, in his clothing)
wraps himself (in his garment or טלית)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The subject is רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא), whose prayer habits were described on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and he would feel around in his garment,
phrases.notes: For example, to remove a louse that was bothering him.

phrases.english: but he would not wrap himself.
phrases.notes: Rewrapping would be a bigger interruption of his prayer.

phrases.english: And when he would yawn,
he would place his hand on his chin.
phrases.notes: So that his open mouth would not be seen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בְּבִגְדוֹ, אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה מִתְעַטֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the report of רבי's conduct earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During תפלה, רבי allowed himself minor physical actions but kept limits: he did not rewrap himself, and he covered his mouth when yawning.

steps.title: A ברייתא about using one's voice in prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי's conduct. It opens by condemning anyone who prays out loud or raises his voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Someone who makes his voice heard in his prayer is one of those with little faith. Someone who raises his voice in his prayer is like the false prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that will challenge רבי's behavior. These opening lines about the voice are background; the clauses that actually clash with רבי come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying audibly suggests the person thinks God cannot hear a quiet prayer, which shows weak faith. Shouting resembles the false prophets, who cried out loudly to their idols. These lines show the ברייתא's general concern: a person's body and voice during תפלה should reflect respect and faith.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (a challenge from a תנאי source)
one who makes his voice heard

steps.confusionAlert: These voice rules are not themselves the contradiction with רבי. They are simply the start of the ברייתא, which is quoted in full.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who makes his voice heard in his prayer —
this person is among those of little faith.
phrases.notes: He acts as if God cannot hear a silent prayer.

phrases.english: One who raises his voice in his prayer
this person is among the false prophets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a ברייתא that will be used to challenge the report of רבי's conduct.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי yawned, sneezed, and spat during תפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנאי source lists improper behaviors during תפלה. Its opening clauses establish the standard of dignity and faith in prayer.

steps.title: The ברייתא condemns yawning, sneezing, and spitting in prayer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It condemns belching and yawning, calls sneezing a bad sign, and compares spitting to spitting before a king. This contradicts what רבי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who belches and yawns is among the arrogant. One who sneezes in his prayer, it is a bad sign for him; some say, it shows he is repulsive. One who spits in his prayer is like spitting in front of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the clauses of the ברייתא that directly clash with רבי's behavior. The challenge is: how could רבי do things that the ברייתא calls disgraceful?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report said רבי belched, yawned, sneezed, and spat during תפלה. This ברייתא treats each of those as improper: arrogance, a bad omen, or disrespect to the King. So the conduct of a great sage seems to contradict a תנאי teaching.

phrases.english: One who belches and yawns —
this person is among the arrogant.
One who sneezes during his prayer —
it is a bad sign for him.
And some say:
it is evident that he is repulsive.
One who spits during his prayer —
it is as if he spat in front of the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַהֵק וּמְפַהֵק — הֲרֵי זֶה מִגַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא; these clauses carry the actual contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's yawning, sneezing, and spitting during תפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא condemns the exact behaviors that רבי was seen doing, so his conduct seems improper.

steps.title: Yawning is solved: involuntary versus deliberate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the yawning and belching contradiction. רבי's yawning was involuntary, while the ברייתא condemns deliberate yawning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, belching and yawning are not a difficulty: here it was involuntary, and there it was deliberate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers part of the challenge. It shows that the yawning contradiction is not a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources describe different situations. רבי yawned because he could not help it, which is not a sign of arrogance. The ברייתא condemns someone who yawns on purpose, which shows a lack of respect.

keyTerms.meaning: involuntarily; when he cannot help it

phrases.english: Granted, belching and yawning
is not difficult:
here it is involuntary,
here it is deliberate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the yawning and belching part of the ברייתא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן… כאן): involuntary versus deliberate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any yawning during תפלה is arrogant, so רבי acted improperly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only deliberate yawning is condemned; involuntary yawning, like רבי's, is acceptable.

steps.title: Sneezing is still a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the sneezing contradiction is not solved. The ברייתא calls sneezing in prayer a bad sign, yet רבי sneezed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But sneezing against sneezing is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the sneezing contradiction remains. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The involuntary-versus-deliberate answer does not work for sneezing. Sneezing is almost always involuntary, yet the ברייתא still calls it a bad sign. So the two sources about sneezing still clash, and a different explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: against sneezing (contrasting one source on sneezing with the other)
a difficulty; it is a problem

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the yawning answer covers sneezing too. Sneezing is naturally involuntary, so the ברייתא's warning cannot be about a deliberate sneeze, and the contradiction remains.

phrases.english: But sneezing against sneezing
is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After solving yawning, the גמרא shows that the same answer does not resolve sneezing.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's sneezing during תפלה versus the ברייתא calling it a bad sign
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sneezing is by nature involuntary, so the 'involuntary versus deliberate' split cannot explain the contradiction.

steps.title: Two kinds of sneezing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now does solve the sneezing contradiction. רבי sneezed from above (the nose), while the ברייתא condemns 'sneezing' from below (passing wind).
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between one sneeze and the other sneeze is also not difficult. Here it means from above, and there it means from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the sneezing problem it had left open and now answers it. The two sources are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'bad sign' refers to passing wind during תפלה, which the גמרא politely calls sneezing 'from below.' רבי's sneeze was a normal sneeze from the nose, 'from above.' So the two sources do not clash.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 5 the sneezing question looked unanswered. Here the גמרא comes back and answers it, so do not think the קשיא remains standing.

phrases.english: Sneezing against sneezing is also not difficult:
here, it is from above (the nose);
there, it is from below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sneezing contradiction left open in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: two different bodily events
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sneezing of any kind during תפלה is a bad sign, so רבי's sneezing is problematic.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sneeze from the nose is fine. Only 'sneezing from below' is a bad sign.

steps.title: רב זירא: sneezing in prayer is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רב זירא reports a tradition from the study hall of רב המנונא. Sneezing from the nose during תפלה is a good sign, because just as he is given relief below, he is given favor above.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב זירא said: I picked up this teaching in the house of רב המנונא, and it is as valuable to me as all my learning: One who sneezes during his prayer, it is a good sign for him. Just as they give him relief below, so they give him favor above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer it just gave. A normal sneeze is not only allowed; it is actually a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves that a sneeze 'from above' is positive, so it cannot be what the ברייתא calls a bad sign. The reasoning is a parallel: the physical relief of the sneeze here mirrors Heavenly favor above. רב זירא valued this teaching very highly.

keyTerms.meaning: I absorbed it / picked it up in passing
it weighs for me / is equal in value to me

phrases.english: As Rav Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אִבַּלְעָא לִי בֵּי רַב הַמְנוּנָא
phrases.english: This matter I absorbed in the house of Rav Hamnuna,
and it is equal for me to all my learning:
One who sneezes in his prayer, it is a good sign for him;

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַטָּה,
phrases.english: just as they give him relief below,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ עוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: so they give him favor above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6's claim that a nasal sneeze is not the bad sign.
steps.raayaObject: That sneezing from the nose during תפלה is not a bad sign.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב זירא's tradition from the house of רב המנונא.

steps.title: The spitting contradiction remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the last open contradiction. רבי spat during תפלה, but the ברייתא compares spitting to spitting before a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: But spitting against spitting is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: Sneezing is now solved, so the גמרא turns to the one problem still left: spitting. This line sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 3, the ברייתא treats spitting in תפלה as a grave insult, like spitting before a king. Yet רבי's conduct included spitting. Unlike yawning and sneezing, the גמרא has not yet explained this.

phrases.english: But spitting against spitting is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After sneezing is solved, the remaining spitting contradiction is raised.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא equates spitting in תפלה with spitting before a king, so how could רבי spit?

steps.title: Spitting into a garment, per רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The spitting contradiction is resolved with רב יהודה's rule. If saliva comes up during תפלה, one lets it soak into his garment, or into his head covering if the garment is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spitting against spitting is also not difficult. It can be explained like רב יהודה, who said: If someone was standing in prayer and saliva came to him, he absorbs it in his garment. And if it is a fine garment, he absorbs it in his head covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the spitting question. רבי's spitting can be explained as the respectful kind, into his clothing, which רב יהודה permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא condemns openly spitting out, which looks like disrespect before the King. Quietly absorbing the saliva into a cloth is a permitted way to deal with it. So רבי's spitting can be read as this permitted kind.

keyTerms.meaning: it is possible to explain like רב יהודה
it happened to come to him
he absorbs it / lets it soak in
head covering (a cloth over the head)

phrases.english: Spitting against spitting is also not difficult;
it is possible as Rav Yehuda says.
For Rav Yehuda said:
If one was standing in prayer
and saliva happened to come to him,
he absorbs it in his garment.
And if it is a fine garment,
he absorbs it in his head covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָק אַרָק נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, אֶפְשָׁר כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spitting קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing manner of action: open spitting versus absorbing into cloth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any spitting during תפלה is like spitting before a king.
steps.terutzMaskana: Absorbing saliva discreetly into a garment or head covering is permitted. רבי's spitting can be explained this way.
steps.whatToRemember: All of רבי's conduct is now reconciled with the ברייתא. Yawning was involuntary, sneezing was from the nose, and spitting was absorbed into cloth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה for anyone who needs to deal with saliva in the middle of שמונה עשרה.

steps.title: רבינא spits behind him, and רב אשי asks why
steps.stepSummary: רבינא, praying behind רב אשי, spat behind himself. רב אשי asked whether he does not hold of רב יהודה's rule to absorb it in the head covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was standing behind רב אשי. Saliva came to him, and he threw it behind him. רב אשי said to him: Does the master not hold of רב יהודה's teaching, that one absorbs it in his head covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests רב יהודה's rule. A student seemed to act against it, and his teacher asked him why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא did not absorb the saliva; he spat it behind him. That looks like ignoring רב יהודה's guidance. The question sets up an explanation of when someone may do this instead.

keyTerms.meaning: does the master not hold this view?

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי אֲחוֹרֵי רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Ravina was standing behind Rav Ashi;
saliva happened to come to him,
and he threw it behind him.
He (Rav Ashi) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Does the master not hold of this teaching of Rav Yehuda,
that he absorbs it in his head covering?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי אֲחוֹרֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story questioning conduct that seems to differ from רב יהודה's rule in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבינא did not follow רב יהודה's rule of absorbing saliva in his head covering.

steps.title: רבינא: I am sensitive
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that he is fastidious. Saliva in his head covering would disturb him, so he spat behind him instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am sensitive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains himself. He does follow רב יהודה, but for a sensitive person the head covering option does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Absorbing saliva in the head covering would bother רבינא so much that it would harm his concentration in תפלה. For such a person, spitting behind him is acceptable. The rule bends to fit a personal sensitivity.

keyTerms.meaning: I am delicate / fastidious in my mind

phrases.english: He (Ravina) said to him:
I am delicate of mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sensitive person, who would be disturbed by saliva in his head covering, may spit behind him.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: praying out loud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the line of the ברייתא that someone who makes his voice heard in תפלה is of little faith. This time it quotes it in order to analyze it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer is among those of little faith.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the first line of the ברייתא from step 2. It is setting up a discussion of when the rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier this line was part of the challenge to רבי. Now the גמרא repeats it for a new purpose: to define its limits. Praying loudly suggests that God only hears a loud voice, which shows weak faith.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes his voice heard

phrases.english: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer
is among those of little faith.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ קוֹלוֹ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְּטַנֵּי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's opening line (step 2) to analyze it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying out loud shows little faith.

steps.title: רב הונא: only if he can concentrate quietly
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the ברייתא. It only applies to someone who can concentrate while whispering. Someone who cannot concentrate quietly may pray aloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They taught this only when he is able to focus his heart in a whisper. But if he is not able to focus his heart in a whisper, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows the ברייתא's rule. The ban on praying aloud is not absolute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of quiet prayer is good כוונה. If whispering ruins a person's focus, then praying aloud is not a sign of weak faith but a way to concentrate, so it is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
They taught this only where he is able
to focus his heart in a whisper;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּלַחַשׁ —
phrases.english: but if he is not able to focus his heart in a whisper,
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying aloud is forbidden only for someone who can concentrate while whispering.

steps.title: Only when praying alone
steps.stepSummary: The permission to pray aloud applies only to someone praying alone. In a congregation, his voice would disturb others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to an individual, but in a congregation, he will come to disturb the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: A second limit is added to the permission. Even someone who needs to pray aloud may do so only by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission from step 13 comes from his personal need for כוונה. But in a ציבור, his loud voice would ruin other people's concentration, so it is not allowed there.
steps.whatToRemember: Praying aloud: forbidden if you can concentrate quietly. Allowed if you cannot, but only when alone, never in a ציבור.

phrases.english: And this applies only to an individual;
but in a congregation,
he will come to disturb the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission to pray aloud is limited to one praying alone, since in a ציבור it disturbs others.

steps.title: רבי אבא avoids רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי אבא wanted to move to ארץ ישראל and avoided his teacher רב יהודה, who held that leaving בבל for ארץ ישראל violates a positive command based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא was avoiding רב יהודה, because he wanted to go up to ארץ ישראל. For רב יהודה said: Anyone who goes up from בבל to ארץ ישראל transgresses a positive command, as it says: 'To Babylonia they shall be brought, and there they shall be until the day I remember them, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will end with a teaching about 'sneezing from below' during תפלה, continuing the earlier sneezing discussion. This opening line explains why רבי אבא did not want to meet his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads the פסוק as a command to stay in בבל until God brings the people back. So he would have objected to רבי אבא's plan, and רבי אבא avoided him to escape that confrontation.

keyTerms.meaning: to go up (move to ארץ ישראל)
my remembering them / my redeeming them

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba was avoiding
Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי לְמִיסַּק לְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: because he wanted to go up to the Land of Israel;
for Rav Yehuda said:
Anyone who goes up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel
transgresses a positive command,
as it is said:
"To Babylonia they shall be brought, and there they shall be

phrases.aramaic: עַד יוֹם פׇּקְדִי אוֹתָם נְאֻם ה׳״.
phrases.english: until the day I remember them, says the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story whose payoff (steps 17–18) is a ruling about 'sneezing from below' during תפלה. It continues the sneezing theme from steps 6–7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל violates a positive command, based on ירמיהו.

steps.title: רבי אבא plans to hear one teaching first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא decides to quietly go hear a teaching from רב יהודה in the study hall before leaving for ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I will go and hear a teaching from him at the assembly hall, and then I will leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא makes his plan. This line sets up the next part of the story, where we will hear what he learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even while avoiding a face-to-face meeting, רבי אבא still wanted one last teaching from his רבי. He would listen unnoticed in the בית ועד and then leave בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: the assembly hall of the Sages

phrases.english: He said: I will go and hear a matter from him
from the assembly hall,
and afterward I will leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי אבא story and sets up the teaching he will hear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבי אבא will hear one more teaching from רב יהודה before leaving.

steps.title: רבי אבא hears a ברייתא about passing wind during prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא finds the תנא reciting a ברייתא before רב יהודה. Someone who passed wind during תפלה waits for the smell to go away, then continues praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found the תנא reciting before רב יהודה: If someone was standing in prayer and passed wind, he waits until the smell goes away, and then he goes back and prays.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the story, רבי אבא arrives at the study hall and hears the teaching being reviewed in front of רב יהודה. The ruling is that after passing wind during תפלה, you wait for the smell to pass and then continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'sneezed' here is a polite way of saying 'passed wind' (from below). Prayer cannot continue while there is a bad smell, so the person pauses until it is gone. This is the first version of the ruling. A second version comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות in the study hall
Literally 'sneezed'; here a polite word for passing wind

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read נתעטש as a normal sneeze through the nose. Here it means passing wind from below. That is why the ברייתא talks about waiting for the smell to go away.

phrases.english: He went, and he found the tanna
who was reciting before Rav Yehuda:
If one was standing in prayer and 'sneezed' (passed wind)
he waits until the odor dissipates
and goes back and prays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבי אבא's plan from step 16 to hear a teaching before leaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who passes wind during תפלה waits until the smell dissipates and then resumes praying.

steps.title: A second version: step back, wait, say a short prayer, and resume
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the ruling. When he feels the need, he steps back four אמות, waits for the smell to pass, says a humble prayer, and continues from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: If someone was standing in prayer and needed to pass wind, he moves back four אמות, passes wind, and waits until the smell goes away. Then he goes back to pray and says: 'Master of the world, You made us with many openings and hollow spaces. Our shame and embarrassment are known to You, in our lives and at our end, when we become maggots and worms.' Then he starts again from the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same ruling, labeled איכא דאמרי. This version adds more details to what the person does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the person knows the urge is coming, so he steps back four אמות first, away from his place of prayer. He also adds a short humble prayer. In it he admits that a human body is weak and embarrassing and asks ה׳ not to judge him harshly. Afterward he picks up at the exact point where he stopped. He does not start the תפלה over.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; introduces a second version of a teaching
Many openings and many hollow spaces (in the human body)
Maggots and worms; what the body becomes after death
From the place where he stopped

phrases.english: Some say:
If one was standing in prayer and felt the need to 'sneeze' (pass wind)
he moves back four cubits,
passes wind, and waits until the odor dissipates,
and goes back to pray, and says:
'Master of the universe, You formed us'
with many openings and many cavities;
it is revealed and known before You
our disgrace and our shame in our lives
and at our end, maggots and worms,'
and he begins from the place where he stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, more detailed version of the ruling in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He steps back four אמות, waits, says the prayer 'רבונו של עולם', and resumes from where he stopped.

steps.title: רבי אבא: this teaching alone was worth the trip
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא declares that even if he had come only to hear this one teaching, it would have been enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If I had come only to hear this one thing, it would have been enough for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי אבא expressing how much he valued the teaching he just heard before leaving for ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא had come to hear something from רב יהודה before leaving (step 16). He found the ברייתא so valuable that it alone justified the visit. The story closes on a note of deep respect for Torah learning, even on a small, practical topic.

keyTerms.meaning: It would be enough for me

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רבי אבא ends here. Before leaving for ארץ ישראל, he heard the rule about passing wind during תפלה: wait for the smell to pass (one version adds stepping back and a humble prayer), then continue from where you stopped.

phrases.english: He said:
Had I come only
to hear this thing, it would have been enough for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ לֹא בָּאתִי אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ דָּבָר זֶה — דַּיִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by giving רבי אבא's reaction to the teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבא valued this teaching so highly that hearing it alone was worth the visit.

steps.title: Saying קריאת שמע in bed under a garment: separate at the neck
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא. Someone lying in bed under his garment, too cold to stick his head out, may press the garment closed at his neck and then say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone was sleeping wrapped in his garment and could not take his head out because of the cold, he presses the garment closed around his neck and reads קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It is about someone in bed with no clothing on except the blanket-garment over him, who wants to say קריאת שמע without getting up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not say קריאת שמע when your mouth is in the same open space as your uncovered body. Pressing the garment tight at the neck creates a barrier between the head and the rest of the body. According to this first opinion, that barrier is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one was sleeping (covered) in his garment,
and he is unable to take out his head
because of the cold,
he makes a barrier with his garment at his neck,
and reads Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא opens a new topic: saying קריאת שמע near uncovered parts of the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrier at the neck is enough to permit saying קריאת שמע in bed.

steps.title: A second opinion: the separation must be at the heart
steps.stepSummary: The יש אומרים opinion says the garment must be pressed closed at the heart, not just at the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: at his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion. It requires the barrier to be lower, at the level of the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion holds that even the heart may not 'see' the uncovered lower body while saying קריאת שמע. So the barrier must go across the chest, between the heart and the lower body. That makes it stricter than the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; a second opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: And some say: at his heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter opinion than step 20 about where the barrier must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The barrier must be at the heart.

steps.title: Challenge to the first opinion: his heart can see his uncovered body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: if the barrier is only at the neck, his heart is still in the same space as his uncovered body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the first תנא, his heart is seeing his nakedness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion. It assumes that the heart must not 'see' the uncovered body, which is exactly what the יש אומרים required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a barrier only at the neck, the heart and the lower body are under the same covering, with nothing between them. The question assumes this should be forbidden. If so, how could the first תנא permit it?

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in the ברייתא
His heart 'sees', meaning it is in the same open space with nothing between

phrases.english: And according to the first tanna,
his heart sees the nakedness!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא הֲרֵי לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning behind the יש אומרים (step 21) to question the first opinion (step 20).
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion, which says a barrier at the neck is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the heart may not see the uncovered body, a barrier at the neck is not enough.

steps.title: Answer: the first opinion permits the heart to see
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא simply holds that it is permitted for the heart to 'see' the uncovered body. Only the mouth must be separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if his heart sees his nakedness, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions really disagree about this exact point. The first תנא does not forbid the heart from seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed everyone agrees the heart may not see. The answer explains that this is the very point the two opinions argue about. For the first תנא, only the mouth (the head) needs to be separated from the uncovered body, so a barrier at the neck works.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions on saying קריאת שמע under a garment. The תנא קמא says a barrier at the neck is enough, because the heart seeing the uncovered body is permitted. The יש אומרים require a barrier at the heart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear argument, 'the heart seeing the uncovered body: permitted or forbidden?', which matters for practical הלכה about saying קריאת שמע in bed.

phrases.english: He holds that if his heart sees the nakedness
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenge's assumption is the very point being argued: the first תנא rejects it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought everyone agrees the heart may not see the uncovered body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא holds the heart seeing is permitted. Only the mouth needs a barrier.

steps.title: A reported way to recite while walking through a filthy alley
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that רבי יוחנן permits a walker to cover his mouth with his hand and recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone was walking through filthy alleys, he places his hand over his mouth and recites קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a ruling about someone walking through filthy alleys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling specifies walking, not standing. It also requires placing a hand over the mouth; the גמרא will now test whether this ruling can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: places his hand over his mouth

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If he was walking through filthy alleys—

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: he places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of separating the mouth from the uncovered body to recitation in a filthy place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person walking through filthy alleys places a hand over his mouth and recites קריאת שמע.

steps.title: A forceful refusal to accept the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he would not follow this ruling even if רבי יוחנן told it to him directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: By God! If רבי יוחנן had said it to me with his own mouth, I would not obey him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא strongly rejects the reported permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not dispute whether the report was heard correctly. His point is that even direct confirmation from רבי יוחנן would not make him follow this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who rejects the ruling

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּפוּמֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yoḥanan had told it to me with his own mouth—
I would not obey him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the permission just reported.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The permission to recite קריאת שמע in filthy alleys.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חסדא gives a forceful refusal here, without yet stating his reasoning.

steps.title: Another version gives the ruling a different source
steps.stepSummary: A second report gives the same ruling, but attributes it to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that someone walking through filthy alleys places his hand over his mouth and recites קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of who transmitted the ruling. This sets up the corresponding version of רב חסדא’s response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical instruction is unchanged. What changes is the chain of names attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage named as the source in this version

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Some say: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
If he was walking through filthy alleys—

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: he places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling after רב חסדא’s rejection and supplies an alternative attribution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same permission to recite קריאת שמע while walking through filthy alleys is attributed here to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: The refusal appears in the second version too
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב חסדא says he would not follow the ruling even if רבי יהושע בן לוי told him directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: By God! If רבי יהושע בן לוי had said it to me with his own mouth, I would not obey him.
steps.whatsHappening: The alternate report repeats רב חסדא’s refusal, naming רבי יהושע בן לוי instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the reported source does not change רב חסדא’s reaction. The disagreement is about following the permission, not merely about which sage said it.

keyTerms.meaning: even if he had said it to me

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי בְּפוּמֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had told it to me with his own mouth—
I would not obey him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רב חסדא’s response to the alternate attribution.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The same permission, now attributed to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חסדא again refuses the ruling without stating a reason at this point.

steps.title: A teaching of רב הונא seems to conflict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts רב הונא’s report with his teaching that a תלמיד חכם may not stand in a filthy place because he will think about תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב הונא really say this? He said that a תלמיד חכם may not stand in a filthy place, because he cannot stand without thinking about תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first report by citing another statement of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even thinking about תורה is a problem in a filthy place, allowing someone to say קריאת שמע there sounds surprising. Notice, though, that the cited prohibition speaks about standing, while the reported permission speaks about walking.

phrases.english: And did Rav Huna say this?
But Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אָסוּר לוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בִּמְקוֹם הַטִּנּוֹפֶת
phrases.english: A Torah scholar is forbidden to stand in a filthy place

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בְּלִי הִרְהוּר תּוֹרָה!
phrases.english: because he cannot stand without thinking about Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the alternate version, tests the original attribution through another teaching of רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא’s transmission of permission to recite קריאת שמע in filthy alleys.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His separate teaching forbids even remaining in a filthy place when doing so will lead a תלמיד חכם to think about תורה.

steps.title: Standing and walking are different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the conflict in רב הונא’s statements by distinguishing standing from walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: Here the person is standing; there the person is walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב הונא by separating the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His prohibition concerns someone standing in a filthy place. The reported permission concerns someone passing through it, so the two statements need not conflict.

phrases.english: This is not difficult: Here it is when one is standing,
and here it is when one is walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — בְּעוֹמֵד, כָּאן — בִּמְהַלֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the apparent conflict in רב הונא’s statements.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by whether the person is standing or walking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to address the same situation in a filthy place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition concerns standing; the reported permission concerns walking.

steps.title: A teaching of רבי יוחנן raises a new challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי יוחנן’s rule excluding the bathhouse and bathroom from places where one may think about תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? רבה בר בר חנה reported in his name: One may think about תורה anywhere except the bathhouse and the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the original report from רבי יוחנן. It brings in his rule about where thinking about תורה is permitted, setting up a closer test of the reported permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted rule shows that רבי יוחנן does place limits on תורה-related thought in unsuitable places. On its own, the quote does not yet settle whether walking through a filthy alley differs from remaining there.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכָל מָקוֹם מוּתָּר לְהַרְהֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: In every place it is permitted to think about words of Torah,
except for the bathhouse and the bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from testing רב הונא’s words to testing the ruling attributed to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reported permission attributed to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching of רבי יוחנן restricts thinking about תורה in unsuitable places, raising doubt about the reported permission.

steps.title: An incident tests the standing-and-walking distinction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers using the earlier distinction again, then cites רבי אבהו stopping קריאת שמע while walking through filthy alleys behind רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too one case is standing and the other is walking—is that so? רבי אבהו was walking behind רבי יוחנן and reciting קריאת שמע. When he reached filthy alleys, he fell silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא prepares the same standing-versus-walking answer, then challenges it with an incident involving an actual walker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו was walking, yet he stopped reciting when he reached the filthy alleys. That makes the earlier distinction harder to use for the report attributed to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage walking behind רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: And if you say: Here too,
one case is standing and the other is walking—
is that so? But Rabbi Abbahu

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: was walking behind Rabbi Yoḥanan
and was reciting Shema.
When he reached filthy alleys, he fell silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי כָּאן בְּעוֹמֵד כָּאן בִּמְהַלֵּךְ — אִינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the answer used for רב הונא can also protect the report attributed to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the standing-versus-walking distinction to רבי יוחנן’s reported permission.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The incident concerns walking, yet רבי אבהו stops reciting קריאת שמע upon reaching filthy alleys.

steps.title: Where should the recitation resume?
steps.stepSummary: After stopping, רבי אבהו asks רבי יוחנן where he should resume קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to רבי יוחנן: To where should I return?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו asks רבי יוחנן what to do after his interruption. The question sets up רבי יוחנן’s response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about where to resume, not an explicit question about whether stopping was correct. The response will show what רבי יוחנן says about the interruption.

phrases.english: He said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
To where should I return?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְהֵיכָן אֶהְדַּר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רבי אבהו’s silence with his practical question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where to resume קריאת שמע after the interruption.

steps.title: A long interruption requires starting again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי אבהו to restart if the interruption lasted long enough to finish all of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you paused long enough to finish all of it, return to the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רבי אבהו’s question about where to resume. He addresses the length of the pause without objecting here to the fact that רבי אבהו stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The instruction applies when the pause lasted as long as reciting the whole קריאת שמע: start over. In this argument, רבי יוחנן’s failure to correct רבי אבהו for stopping also strengthens the challenge to the reported permission to recite while walking through filthy alleys.

keyTerms.meaning: long enough to finish all of it

steps.whatToRemember: The standing-versus-walking answer resolves the question about רב הונא. The רבי אבהו incident seems to show that רבי יוחנן also requires stopping. The next step answers this: רבי יוחנן's instruction was given only according to רבי אבהו's own view.

phrases.english: He said to him: If you delayed
long enough to finish all of it—
return to the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבהו’s question and completes the incident used to challenge the reported permission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the interruption lasted long enough to finish the entire קריאת שמע, resume from the beginning.

steps.title: A conditional answer, not agreement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answered רבי אבהו according to רבי אבהו’s view, without accepting that view himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he said to him: I do not hold that way. But according to your view, if you paused long enough to finish all of it, return to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן’s earlier answer. His instruction about restarting קריאת שמע was conditional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו had stopped reciting, but רבי יוחנן did not agree that he needed to stop. רבי יוחנן’s point was: if you follow your view and stop, a long enough pause requires you to restart.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not hold that view

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
For my part, I do not hold that view,
but according to you, who do hold that view,

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: if you paused long enough to finish all of it,
return to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by reinterpreting רבי יוחנן's reply in step 33 as conditional, so the permission attributed to him in step 24 stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Interprets an instruction as conditional on the listener’s position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן’s instruction seemed to show that he agreed רבי אבהו had to stop.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן could give רבי אבהו a restart rule without agreeing that he had to stop.

steps.title: Sources are introduced for both sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports רב הונא and another supports רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with רב הונא, and it was taught in accordance with רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move: it will present a teaching supporting each side. This line announces the two sources before quoting them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement remains in place. The next two steps show what each supporting ברייתא actually says.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who reported the permission (step 24)

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Huna,
and it was taught in accordance with Rav Hisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא, תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי יוחנן’s answer to presenting sources for the underlying disagreement.

steps.title: A teaching supports reciting while walking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב הונא by allowing a walker in filthy alleyways to cover his mouth and recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with רב הונא: One walking through filthy alleyways places his hand over his mouth and recites קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first promised ברייתא. It gives a way to keep reciting while walking through filthy alleyways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching supports רב הונא’s walking case. It does not say to continue without taking any precaution: the person covers his mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: places his hand over his mouth

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Huna:
One walking through filthy alleyways—
places his hand over his mouth
and recites Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the first of the two promised supporting teachings.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא’s position in the case of someone walking through filthy alleyways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא instructing the walker to cover his mouth and recite קריאת שמע.

steps.title: A teaching supports stopping the recitation
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא supports רב חסדא: one may not begin קריאת שמע there and must stop if already reciting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with רב חסדא: One walking through filthy alleyways may not recite קריאת שמע. Moreover, if he was already reciting, he stops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second promised ברייתא. It rules against reciting קריאת שמע in the alleyways, even when the recitation began earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case concerns starting to recite there. The added case makes the rule stronger: someone who is already reciting must interrupt.

keyTerms.meaning: and not only that, but also

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Hisda:
If he was walking through filthy alleyways—
he may not recite Shema,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הָיָה קוֹרֵא וּבָא —
phrases.english: and moreover, if he was already reciting as he went—
he stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing supporting teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא’s position that recitation must stop in filthy alleyways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding recitation there and requiring an ongoing recitation to stop.

steps.title: What if he kept reciting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about someone who did not stop as the second ברייתא required.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not stop—what then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about a person who continued reciting. The question follows the second ברייתא’s instruction to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated what the person should do. The גמרא now asks how to view someone who did the opposite.

phrases.english: If he did not stop—what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about failure to follow the stopping rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the גמרא describes someone who continues reciting when the ברייתא says to stop.

steps.title: A verse condemns continuing
steps.stepSummary: רבי מיאשה בן בנו של רבי יהושע בן לוי applies a harsh verse to the person who did not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מיאשה, grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, said: Of him Scripture says, ‘Moreover, I gave them statutes that were not good and laws by which they could not live.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse applied to the person who kept reciting. The answer expresses serious disapproval, rather than giving a new place to resume.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person may think continuing קריאת שמע is always the right thing to do. This response says that, in this case, continuing turns his recitation into wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who cites the first verse
laws by which they could not live

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָאשָׁה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meyasha, grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said:
Of him Scripture says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְגַם אֲנִי נָתַתִּי לָהֶם חֻקִּים לֹא טוֹבִים
phrases.english: ‘Moreover, I gave them statutes that were not good
and laws by which they could not live.’

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָאשָׁה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about someone who did not stop.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A severe verse is applied to the person who continued reciting.

steps.title: Continuing is described as drawing iniquity
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי applies a different verse to the same conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: ‘Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity.’
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives another verse for the person who kept reciting. He describes that choice as drawing wrongdoing upon oneself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new case or a new instruction about where to resume. It adds another way to express why continuing was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who cites the second verse

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
‘Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a different verse describing the same failure to stop.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי applies a verse about drawing iniquity to someone who continued reciting.

steps.title: Continuing is described as contempt
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a third verse, describing the conduct as contempt for God’s word.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said it is from here: ‘For he has shown contempt for the word of the Lord.’
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה supplies one more verse about the person who did not stop. This verse describes the conduct as showing contempt for God’s word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the previous verse, this addresses the choice to keep reciting in the filthy place. It does not change the practical instruction in the ברייתא: stop reciting.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who cites the third verse
he has shown contempt for the word of the Lord

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא brought a ברייתא for each side of the walking case. Its closing verses warn against continuing קריאת שמע when one is required to stop.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said it is from here:
‘For he has shown contempt for the word of the Lord.’

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third verse for the same conduct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אדא בר אהבה applies a verse about contempt for God’s word to someone who continued reciting.

steps.title: What is the reward for stopping?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reward a person receives for stopping קריאת שמע when required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he stopped, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: After discussing someone who did not stop, the גמרא now asks about someone who did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statements described the seriousness of continuing. This question shifts attention to the person who follows the instruction.

phrases.english: And if he stopped, what is his reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It turns from the consequences of not stopping to the reward for stopping.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward is associated with stopping the recitation as required?

steps.title: A verse promises long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו applies a verse about long life to the person who stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: About him, the verse says, “And through this matter you will prolong your days.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by applying a verse to the person who stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse supplies the promised reward: long life. רבי אבהו applies it here to stopping when required.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who gives this answer

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא contrasts failing to stop with stopping: רבי אבהו associates stopping with the verse’s promise of long life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
About him, the verse says:
“And through this matter you will prolong your days.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question about the reward for stopping.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבהו applies the verse’s promise of long life to the person who stopped.

steps.title: A garment tied around the waist permits recitation
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא permits קריאת שמע when a person’s garment is tied around the waist.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If his garment was tied around his waist, he may recite קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new clothing case. רב הונא states when a person wearing a garment around the waist may recite קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment’s position is the key detail: it is tied around the waist. The statement gives permission to recite קריאת שמע in that case.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: If his garment was
tied around his waist—
he may recite Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It leaves the discussion of stopping and begins a separate rule about clothing during קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person whose garment is tied around the waist may recite קריאת שמע.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the waist-garment rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the same permission for a garment of cloth, leather, or sackcloth tied around the waist.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught: If his garment of cloth, leather, or sackcloth was tied around his waist, he may recite קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב הונא’s rule. It lists several garment materials and gives the same permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the key condition: the garment is tied around the waist. Its ruling matches רב הונא’s, so it serves as support for his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: this was also taught; introduces a supporting teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רב הונא: a garment tied around the waist permits קריאת שמע, whether it is made of cloth, leather, or sackcloth.

phrases.english: This was also taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה טַלִּיתוֹ שֶׁל בֶּגֶד וְשֶׁל עוֹר
phrases.english: If his garment was of cloth or of leather
or of sackcloth, tied around his waist—
he may recite Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supports רב הונא’s rule with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא’s permission to recite קריאת שמע with a garment tied around the waist.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא allowing recitation when a cloth, leather, or sackcloth garment is tied around the waist.
